hmmt-feb-2017-team-01.prompt: Let $P(x),Q(x)$ be nonconstant polynomials with real number coefficients. Prove that if $\lfloor P(y)\rfloor=\lfloor Q(y)\rfloor$ for all real numbers $y$, then $P(x)=Q(x)$ for all real numbers $x$.
hmmt-feb-2017-team-01.answer: $P-Q$ is bounded, hence a constant $c$; if $c\ne0$, pick $x_0$ with $Q(x_0)+c$ an integer to get a contradiction.

hmmt-feb-2017-team-02.prompt: Does there exist a two-variable polynomial $P(x,y)$ with real number coefficients such that $P(x,y)$ is positive exactly when $x$ and $y$ are both positive?
hmmt-feb-2017-team-02.answer: No such polynomial exists (look at the lowest-degree homogeneous part of $P$).

hmmt-feb-2017-team-03.prompt: A polyhedron has $7n$ faces. Show that there exist $n+1$ of the polyhedron's faces that all have the same number of edges.
hmmt-feb-2017-team-03.answer: By Euler's formula $2\le F-\frac16\sum k\,a_k$; if each $a_k\le n$ this sum is at most $0$.

hmmt-feb-2017-team-04.prompt:
Let $w=w_1w_2\dots w_n$ be a word. Define a substring of $w$ to be a word of the form $w_iw_{i+1}\dots w_{j-1}w_j$, for some pair of positive integers $1\le i\le j\le n$. Show that $w$ has at most $n$ distinct palindromic substrings.

For example, $aaaaa$ has $5$ distinct palindromic substrings, and $abcata$ has $5$ ($a,b,c,t,ata$).
hmmt-feb-2017-team-04.answer: Give each palindrome its leftmost occurrence; distinct palindromes then have distinct right endpoints.

hmmt-feb-2017-team-05.prompt: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. The altitudes $BE$ and $CF$ intersect at the orthocenter $H$, and point $O$ denotes the circumcenter. Point $P$ is chosen so that $\angle APH=\angle OPE=90^\circ$, and point $Q$ is chosen so that $\angle AQH=\angle OQF=90^\circ$. Lines $EP$ and $FQ$ meet at point $T$. Prove that points $A,T,O$ are collinear.
hmmt-feb-2017-team-05.answer: $T$ is the radical center of the circles with diameters $OE$, $OF$, $AH$, so it lies on their radical axis $OX$ ($X$ the foot from $O$ to $EF$), which is line $AO$ because $AO\perp EF$.

hmmt-feb-2017-team-06.prompt: Let $r$ be a positive integer. Show that if a graph $G$ has no cycles of length at most $2r$, then it has at most $|V|^{2016}$ cycles of length exactly $2016r$, where $|V|$ denotes the number of vertices in the graph $G$.
hmmt-feb-2017-team-06.answer: Between two vertices there is at most one path of length $r$; a cycle of length $2016r$ is determined by every $r$-th vertex along it, giving at most $|V|^{2016}$ choices.

hmmt-feb-2017-team-07a.prompt: Let $p$ be a prime. A *complete residue class modulo $p$* is a set containing at least one element equivalent to $k\pmod p$ for all $k$. Show that there exists an $n$ such that the $n$th row of Pascal's triangle (the numbers $\binom n0,\binom n1,\dots,\binom nn$) forms a complete residue class modulo $p$.
hmmt-feb-2017-team-07a.answer: Take $n=p^2-2$; Lucas's theorem gives $\binom nk\equiv(-1)^{q+r}(r+1)$ for $k=pq+r$.

hmmt-feb-2017-team-07b.prompt: Let $p$ be a prime. A *complete residue class modulo $p$* is a set containing at least one element equivalent to $k\pmod p$ for all $k$. Show that there exists an $n\le p^2$ such that the $n$th row of Pascal's triangle (the numbers $\binom n0,\binom n1,\dots,\binom nn$) forms a complete residue class modulo $p$.

hmmt-feb-2017-team-08.prompt: Does there exist an irrational number $\alpha>1$ such that $$\lfloor\alpha^n\rfloor\equiv0\pmod{2017}$$ for all integers $n\ge1$?

hmmt-feb-2017-team-09.prompt: Let $n$ be a positive odd integer greater than $2$, and consider a regular $n$-gon $\mathcal G$ in the plane centered at the origin. Let a *subpolygon* $\mathcal G'$ be a polygon with at least $3$ vertices whose vertex set is a subset of that of $\mathcal G$. Say $\mathcal G'$ is *well-centered* if its centroid is the origin. Also, say $\mathcal G'$ is *decomposable* if its vertex set can be written as the disjoint union of regular polygons with at least $3$ vertices. Show that all well-centered subpolygons are decomposable if and only if $n$ has at most two distinct prime divisors.
hmmt-feb-2017-team-09.answer: Work in $\mathbb Z_n$. For $\le2$ primes: vanishing sums are integer (then nonnegative) combinations of $p$-gons and $q$-gons via $\Phi_n$. For $\ge3$ primes: $T=(\bigcup S_j)\setminus S'$ is a well-centered, non-decomposable set.

hmmt-feb-2017-team-10.prompt: Let $LBC$ be a fixed triangle with $LB=LC$, and let $A$ be a variable point on arc $LB$ of its circumcircle. Let $I$ be the incenter of $\triangle ABC$ and $AK$ the altitude from $A$. The circumcircle of $\triangle IKL$ intersects lines $KA$ and $BC$ again at $U\ne K$ and $V\ne K$. Finally, let $T$ be the projection of $I$ onto line $UV$. Prove that the line through $T$ and the midpoint of $IK$ passes through a fixed point as $A$ varies.
hmmt-feb-2017-team-10.answer: The fixed point is the midpoint $M$ of arc $BC$ not containing $L$: the line is the Simson line of $I$ in $\triangle KUV$ and passes through $D$ (incircle touch point) and $M$.
